meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_65_packages.json, all reference===65 edges from torahData.js, and full source text torah_65.txt. For each bechina statement in the source text (using language בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, הוּא, זֶה בְּחִינַת), verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset and is assigned to a package. Only explicit bechina declarations were counted — not verse citations, narrative elaborations, or implied parallels. The proposed Package 5 (שדה/נשמות) from torah_65_new_packages.json is assumed here; nodes assigned to 'package_id: 5_proposed' belong to that new package pending acceptance.

Boaz belongs in the נפש package (Package 3) because his defining relationship in this Torah is as the sekhel whose illumination enables the nefesh (Ruth) to gather rightly. concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 49 states 'הָעֵינַיִם נִקְרָאִים נְעָרִים' — the formula נִקְרָא IS bechina language. However, this is a homiletic bridge within the biblical commentary on Ruth 2:9, playing on the word 'נְעָרִים' from the verse to mean both 'lads' (farm hands) and 'servants of the sekhel' (eyes as agents of intellect). The operational concept throughout the Torah is עֵינַיִם/רְאוּת which appears in eitza edges. 'נערים' as a term is fully explained as a synonym for the eyes/sight in this context, not establishing a new conceptual domain. Excluded.

Line 57 states 'שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינוֹת אֶצְבַּע אֱלֹקִים' (citing Exodus 31). This IS a bechina statement. However, in Torah #65 the Torah/Torah-renewal appears only through eitza chains (the bitul→reshimu→חידושי-אורייתא flow) and has no dedicated bechina package. The אצבע אלקים = Torah equation is a culminating image in the final verse of the Torah's commentary. It reinforces the eschatological mareh/zarihah theme. Provisionally excluded from additions as it would belong in a Torah-novelty sub-concept of Package 2 (שמחה/קבלת התורה) where Torah-renewal already lives, but it lacks a direct bechina connection to any node in that package — the text says the mareh/zarihah IS the Torah, using 'בְּחִינוֹת', but this is directed at Torah as a whole rather than at קבלת התורה specifically. Could be added as a secondary addition to Package 2 in a future pass.

Line 35 cites 'אֶרֶץ פְּרִי לִמְלֵחָה' as illustrative proof for the already-captured bechina מליחות = יסורין (edge 1367). This is a verse citation used as supporting proof text, not a new independent bechina node. The concept it illustrates (deficient sekhel = saltiness = suffering) is fully captured by edge 1367. Excluded.

הרשימו appears multiple times in section ד as the mechanism by which chidushei Torah arrive, stated in causal terms ('מן הרשימו שנשאר מן הביטול'). No sentence declares 'רשימו הוא בחינת X' using explicit bechina language. It functions exclusively as an eitza-chain node (bitul → reshimu → chidushei Torah). Excluded from additions as a bechina node.

Sections ג-ד describe the מוח as the vessel (כלי) of the sekhel and the anatomical seat of pain. The text uses the formula 'עִקַּר הַהַרְגָּשָׁה הוּא בַּמֹּחַ' — a factual claim about the physical location of pain-sensation, not a bechina declaration of equivalent natures between two concepts. The מוח serves as a physical substrate in an extended physiological analogy (closing eyes to concentrate vision = bitul to reach takhlit). It appears in eitza contexts ('כשחוזר השכל מהביטול אל המוח') as a vessel, not as a bechina-equivalent node. Excluded.

Line 8 states 'בְּכִי הוּא קִלְקוּל הָרְאוּת' — this uses the formula הוּא and could be a bechina statement. However, it functions as an explanation/definition within the שדה בוכים declaration rather than establishing בכי as an independent concept-node. The בכי = ruination-of-sight equation is the explanation FOR why the שדה בוכים is what it is, not a separate bechina concept. It is embedded within the שדה בוכים entry (added above). Treated as part of שדה בוכים rather than a separate addition.
